Budgeting, saving, calculating EMI/returns, comparing products, reading statements.
Long-term thinking, disciplined spending, willingness to plan.

NABARD (agriculture and rural), SIDBI (small industry), EXIM Bank (foreign trade), NaBFID (infrastructure).
RBI (banks, NBFCs, payment systems), SEBI (securities, mutual funds), IRDAI (insurance), PFRDA (pension), IFSCA (GIFT City), NABARD, NHB (housing finance sector development).
India Post — world's largest postal network; also offers small savings schemes, Postal Life Insurance, India Post Payments Bank and money transfer — vital for rural financial inclusion.
Commitment of money or resources today to acquire assets that are expected to generate income or appreciation in the future.
Financial investment (shares, bonds, FDs, mutual funds) vs real investment (land, gold, buildings, machinery).
The possibility that actual returns differ from expected returns. Return: gain or loss on an investment (income + capital appreciation).

Higher expected return means higher risk. Low risk: savings account, FD, government bonds, PPF; moderate: debt mutual funds, corporate bonds, gold; high: equity shares, equity funds, derivatives, crypto.
Market risk, credit/default risk, interest-rate risk, inflation risk, liquidity risk, reinvestment risk, currency risk, political risk. Systematic (non-diversifiable) vs unsystematic (diversifiable).
Real return ≈ nominal return − inflation.

Assessing an investor's risk capacity (financial ability to bear loss) and risk tolerance (psychological willingness) to match with suitable investments — required by SEBI for advisers and distributors (suitability).
A questionnaire (age, income, dependents, goals, horizon, reaction to a 20% fall).

flashcards.back: Personalisation, speed, lower cost, inclusion of small investors, dynamic updating of profile.
Data privacy, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency ("black box"), over-reliance, regulatory accountability, quality of data. Human oversight remains necessary.

flashcards.back: Builds knowledge → changes behaviour → good decisions → financial resilience and wellbeing (ability to meet obligations, absorb shocks, achieve goals and have financial freedom).

Ensures goal achievement, avoids financial stress, secures family, builds wealth through disciplined saving, reduces tax, prepares for contingencies.
Answer queries about savings, budgeting, loans, frauds 24x7, in multiple (regional) languages — improving reach to the rural and first-time users.

Hallucination or incorrect advice, privacy concerns, digital divide, over-reliance, need for human help and grievance channel.
Accepting deposits; lending/advances (loans, overdraft, cash credit, discounting of bills).

Public sector (12 PSBs after mergers), private sector, foreign banks.

DD, pay order, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI; cheque collection.

Fixed monthly instalments for a fixed tenor (6 months to 10 years).
Nominee receives deposit on death of the holder; nominee is a trustee, not necessarily the owner.
Accounts inoperative for 10 years go to the RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund; people can reclaim via banks (UDGAM portal to find unclaimed deposits).

flashcards.back: Prevent money laundering, terror financing, identity theft and fraud; know customer's transaction profile.
Aadhaar, passport, driving licence, voter ID, NREGA job card, letter from the National Population Register. PAN (or Form 60) is required for specified transactions.
Customer Acceptance Policy, Customer Identification Procedures, Monitoring of Transactions, Risk Management.
Every 2 years (high risk), 8 years (medium), 10 years (low risk).
Secured (home, vehicle, gold, FD, loan against property) vs Unsecured (personal loan, credit card, education loan up to a limit).
Home, auto, education, personal, gold, agricultural (Kisan Credit Card), MSME, business, microfinance, loan against securities.
Permission to withdraw more than the balance up to a limit. Cash credit (CC): working capital against stock/receivables.

Pay EMIs/bills on time, keep low utilisation, avoid multiple applications, maintain old accounts, check report for errors.
Based on bureau data (history) — excludes "credit invisible" people (no history).

flashcards.back: Logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, neural networks; automated underwriting, document OCR, fraud checks.

Bias and discrimination, lack of explainability, privacy, data misuse, over-lending, predatory digital apps. RBI Digital Lending Directions — loans only through RBI-regulated entities; direct disbursal to borrower's bank account; Key Fact Statement (KFS); cooling-off period; no automatic limit increase without consent;
Internet banking, mobile banking (apps), SMS banking, phone banking, ATMs, POS, UPI, kiosks, WhatsApp banking.
Convenience, speed, 24x7, lower cost, transparency, reduced cash handling and corruption, record for tax. Risks: phishing, vishing, skimming, SIM swap, malware, fake apps, cyber attacks.
Never share OTP, CVV or PIN; use strong passwords and two-factor authentication; avoid public Wi-Fi; check URL (https); regularly check statements; enable alerts.

Zero liability if the fraud is due to bank's fault or third-party breach and reported within 3 working days; limited liability (Rs 5,000–25,000) if reported in 4–7 days; beyond 7 days as per bank policy.

Fingerprint, iris, face, voice (voiceprint). Voice recognition verifies a customer on phone banking or voice-based UPI; facial recognition unlocks banking apps, supports video KYC and liveness detection (to stop deepfakes).

Fast, convenient, hard to forget/steal. Risks: spoofing, deepfakes, privacy and data protection (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023), false rejections, exclusion of people with disabilities. Usually used as part of multi-factor authentication.

(1) complain to the bank's branch/ nodal/ principal nodal officer (written, with acknowledgement); (2) if no reply within 30 days or unsatisfied — approach the RBI Ombudsman under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (single portal cms.rbi.org.in, email and toll-free 14448, free of cost);
Unauthorised transactions, ATM failures, delay in credit, loan recovery harassment, cheque dishonour, charges, KYC issues, digital lending app harassment.
Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act — penalty up to 2 years imprisonment or fine up to twice the cheque amount, after statutory notice (30 days), reply time 15 days.

Real-time transaction monitoring; anomaly detection (unusual amount, location, device); supervised ML (classification of fraud vs genuine), unsupervised ML (clustering), graph analytics (mule account networks), behavioural biometrics, risk scoring of every UPI/card transaction in milliseconds; reducing false positives.
Money laundering = disguising proceeds of crime as legitimate. Stages: placement, layering, integration.
Name screening against sanctions lists, network analysis, auto-generation of alerts and STRs, reduce false alerts, RegTech/SupTech; MuleHunter.AI.
Cash, cheque, demand draft, cards, wallets, bank transfers, UPI, e-mandates, CBDC.
Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, JCB, Discover, RuPay (global tie-ups).
Fedwire and CHIPS (USA), CHAPS (UK), TARGET2/T2 (Eurozone), CIPS (China), BOJ-NET (Japan).
SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area), Faster Payments (UK), PIX (Brazil), FedNow (USA), PayNow (Singapore); international UPI linkages.
PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Alipay, WeChat Pay, Stripe, Wise.
Correspondent banking (Nostro/Vostro accounts), CLS Bank for forex settlement (payment vs payment). Remittances (Western Union, MoneyGram).
Cheques, demand drafts, pay orders, money orders.
RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI, NACH, AePS, NFS, BBPS, NUUP (USSD), cards, PPIs.
Launched 2010; channel: mobile, internet, ATM, SMS; works on holidays.
National Unified USSD Platform — dial \*99# for banking services without internet; supports balance, fund transfer, mini statement, in many languages.
National Automated Clearing House — bulk credit (salaries, dividends, pensions, subsidy) and bulk debit (EMIs, SIPs, insurance premiums); replaced ECS.

Allows cash withdrawal, balance enquiry, mini statement, fund transfer, using Aadhaar number and fingerprint/iris at micro-ATMs of business correspondents; vital for rural and Jan Dhan accounts; risks of biometric cloning fraud.

The user speaks a command ("Pay Rs 500 to Ramesh") — speech recognition + NLP convert it into a payment instruction; UPI-based voice assistants in regional languages (e.g. Hello UPI, Google Assistant and Alexa-based payments); helpful for first-time and visually-impaired users.
Fingerprint, face, iris, voice, behavioural patterns (typing speed, swipe pattern). Aadhaar-based authentication, Face ID and fingerprint for apps and UPI PIN replacement.
Voiceprint matching, liveness detection, anti-spoofing, anomaly detection, adaptive (risk-based) authentication.

flashcards.front: AI-Powered Voice Payments and Biometric Authentication — Concerns
flashcards.back: Deepfake voice cloning, replay attacks, privacy of biometric data (DPDP Act 2023), misrecognition, accents; need for MFA and consent.
Paperless identity verification using Aadhaar OTP or biometric through UIDAI; fast onboarding; the customer consents; used by banks, mutual funds, insurers, telcos.

Online electronic signature service using Aadhaar authentication — legally valid under the IT Act, 2000 (Section 3A, Second Schedule); used for loan agreements, account opening, GST/ITR filing; Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) is a different (cryptographic key-based) method.

The largest network of shared ATMs in India — interlinks banks' ATMs so customers can use any bank's ATM; operated by NPCI since 2009 (launched by IDRBT in 2004); also supports cardless cash withdrawal and cash deposit.

Funds transfer in real time, settled individually (gross) in RBI's books; min Rs 2 lakh with no upper limit; available 24x7x365 since December 2020; charges as per RBI cap; suitable for large-value transactions; irrevocable; needs beneficiary name, account no., IFSC.

Deferred net settlement in half-hourly batches (24x7 since 16 December 2019); no minimum and no maximum limit (bank-wise limits can apply); used for retail transfers; funds returned if undelivered within two hours.
RTGS — large value, continuous gross, immediate; NEFT — retail, batches, net settlement.

Buying/selling currencies; spot (T+2), forward, swap; nostro and vostro accounts; SWIFT messages; Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) — resident individuals can remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year for permitted purposes; CLS settles forex payment-versus-payment to reduce Herstatt (settlement) risk;

The delivery of securities against payment — through clearing corporations (NSCCL, ICCL) and depositories (NSDL, CDSL); India follows T+1 rolling settlement for equities (since January 2023; optional T+0 introduced in 2024 for select shares); DvP (delivery versus payment);
AI that understands human language (text and speech).

Chatbots to answer queries (transaction status, refunds, failed payments, limits, charges); voice assistants; sentiment analysis of complaints; intent classification and automated ticket routing; multilingual translation (Bhashini); automated dispute resolution and chargeback explanations; conversational payments (Hello UPI);

flashcards.front: NLP in Digital Payment Queries — Benefits
flashcards.back: 24x7 support, lower cost, quick response, regional-language access, consistency.
Ambiguity and slang, code-mixing (Hinglish), accuracy, privacy of financial data, hallucination, need for human escalation, security of conversational channels (vishing).
Minimum balance Rs 500; interest paid annually; cheque and ATM facility; single or joint (up to 3 adults); interest up to a limit is exempt under Section 80TTA (old regime).
Tenure 5 years; minimum Rs 100 per month (multiples of Rs 10); interest compounded quarterly; loan facility up to 50% after 12 instalments; premature closure allowed after 3 years.
Tenures of 1, 2, 3 and 5 years; minimum Rs 1,000; interest compounded quarterly and paid annually; the 5-year TD qualifies for Sec 80C deduction.
5-year scheme paying a monthly interest; maximum investment Rs 9 lakh (single) and Rs 15 lakh (joint); minimum Rs 1,000; premature closure after 1 year (with deduction).
Certificate that doubles the investment in a fixed period (about 9 years 7 months at current rates); minimum Rs 1,000, no maximum limit; can be encashed after 2½ years; no 80C benefit; no TDS.
A 2-year scheme for women and girls (2023–2025), closed for new deposits after 31 March 2025.

Launched 2018; a payments bank under the Department of Posts (100% government-owned); doorstep banking via postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks with micro-ATMs and Aadhaar-enabled services; zero-balance accounts; DBT payments; bill payments; cannot lend; deposits up to Rs 2 lakh per customer.

Money Order (MO) — traditional postal remittance; electronic Money Order (eMO) and Instant Money Order (iMO); International Money Transfer Service via Western Union (inward); IPPB remittances; India Post Payments through DAKPAY app.

flashcards.front: AI for Fraud Detection and Account Security for Postal Ac... — Challenges
flashcards.back: Legacy systems, low digital literacy, rural connectivity, privacy.
A compulsory/voluntary savings scheme to provide retirement benefits through accumulation of contributions plus interest.

Declared every year by the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) and approved by the Finance Ministry; historically around 8–8.8% in recent years (for example 8.25% for FY 2024–25); credited annually; tax-free within limits (interest on employee contribution above Rs 2.5 lakh per year is taxable).
Full withdrawal at retirement (58 years) or after 2 months of unemployment; partial withdrawals for marriage, education, illness, home purchase/construction.

EPFO invests mainly in government securities, state development loans, public sector bonds and AAA-rated corporate bonds; since 2015 up to 15% in equity ETFs (Nifty/Sensex-based); investment pattern notified by the Ministry of Labour/Finance; trusts for exempted establishments must follow norms.

EPFO has become one of the world's largest social security organisations — over 7 crore active contributors and a corpus of more than Rs 25 lakh crore; digitisation through UAN, UMANG app, online claims, auto-settlement.
Regular income after retirement. Pillars: (1) mandatory (EPF/EPS), (2) voluntary (NPS, PPF), (3) social assistance (NSAP, APY).
Mandatory, locked till 60 (restricted withdrawal); Tier II: voluntary, flexible withdrawal.
The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) has been offered from 1 April 2025 as an option alongside NPS (assured payout on 25+ years of service).
For unorganised sector aged 18–40; guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000–5,000 from age 60; government co-contribution earlier for eligible subscribers.
PMSBY, PM-SYM, annuity plans from LIC and private insurers, pension plans of mutual funds, EPS, Old Pension Scheme (OPS) for government employees before 2004 (defined benefit).
DB — fixed pension formula by employer/state (OPS); DC — pension depends on contributions and returns (NPS).
New tax regime (default; lower slab rates; most deductions not allowed) and Old tax regime (higher slab rates but deductions and exemptions available).
Additional deduction up to Rs 50,000 for NPS. 80CCD(2): employer's contribution to NPS.

80E (interest on education loan — no limit, 8 years), 80EEA/24(b) (home loan interest up to Rs 2 lakh), 80TTA/TTB (savings interest: Rs 10,000/ Rs 50,000 for seniors), HRA, LTA, standard deduction (Rs 75,000 in the new regime for salaried — as per the latest changes).

Income above basic exemption limit; also in specified cases (foreign assets, high deposits, TDS thresholds). Due date: 31 July (non-audit individuals) of the assessment year; belated/revised returns allowed with fees.
PAN, Aadhaar, Form 16 (salary), Form 26AS / AIS / TIS (tax credit statement), bank statements, interest certificates, investment proofs, capital gains statements.
Gross total income − deductions = taxable income; apply slab rates; add surcharge and 4% health and education cess; subtract rebate (Sec 87A) and TDS/advance tax → tax payable/refund.
A contract (policy) in which the insurer agrees to compensate the insured for specified losses in return for a premium. It transfers risk from an individual to the pool.

Insurer, insured/policyholder, premium, sum assured/ sum insured, policy, nominee, beneficiary, claim, rider, surrender value, maturity, lapse and revival, grace period (30 days for annual premium; 15 for monthly).
Risk protection, certainty, savings, capital formation, social security, credit support, encourages investment (insurers hold large investments).

Life insurance and General (non-life) insurance (health, motor, property, marine, etc.).
Pays a sum on death or maturity; contract of assurance; insurable interest at inception.
Pure protection, high cover at low premium, no maturity benefit (except return-of-premium variants); riders for critical illness and accidental death; best for earning members.
Savings + protection; pays sum assured on maturity or death; with/without profit (bonus); money-back plan pays survival benefits at intervals.
Cover for entire life (up to 99/100 years); maturity at death or at 100.
Build a retirement corpus; deferred annuity vs immediate annuity; annuity options (life, joint life, with return of purchase price).
Age, health, sum assured, term, lifestyle (smoking), occupation, gender; mortality tables.

Covers hospitalisation and medical costs; indemnity (reimbursement) plans — pay actual expenses up to sum insured (mediclaim); fixed-benefit plans — pay a fixed sum on diagnosis (critical illness, hospital cash).
Individual, family floater, senior citizen, group (employer), top-up/super top-up, critical illness, personal accident, maternity, disease-specific, government schemes.
Cashless vs reimbursement claim (network hospitals — TPA), waiting periods (initial 30 days; pre-existing diseases up to 3 years — reduced from 4 years;
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for eligible poor families; extended to all senior citizens aged 70+ in 2024), CGHS, ESIC for employees, PMSBY and PMJJBY.
Section 80D (see Unit 4).
Adequate cover (metro cities Rs 10 lakh+), network hospitals, claim settlement ratio, no room-rent cap, lifetime renewability, waiting periods.

Covers loss/damage to physical property — fire and allied perils policy, Standard Fire and Special Perils, householder's/ home insurance (structure + contents; earthquake, flood, theft, burglary), commercial property, marine cargo, engineering insurance (CAR, EAR), machinery breakdown, consequential loss (business interruption).
Insured value (market vs reinstatement value), average clause (underinsurance penalty), deductibles, exclusions (war, nuclear, wear and tear), survey by a licensed surveyor after loss.

Use of AI, OCR, RPA and straight-through processing — customers upload photos/documents on the app; AI extracts data, image-recognition estimates vehicle damage, checks policy coverage and fraud indicators, approves small claims in minutes and sends payment directly;

Started 1884 — the oldest life insurance scheme in India; for government and semi-government employees, teachers and bank employees etc.; Rural Postal Life Insurance (RPLI): 1995 for rural population;
Long-term loan (tenure up to 30 years) to buy, construct, extend or repair a house; secured by mortgage of the property; LTV (Loan-to-Value) up to 75–90% depending on the loan amount (RBI norms).

EMI, down payment, processing fee, floating/fixed rate, prepayment, balance transfer, top-up loan, tax benefits (principal Sec 80C; interest Sec 24(b) up to Rs 2 lakh on self-occupied property in the old regime).
Launched June 2015 with the vision "Housing for All".
Family should not own a pucca house; women ownership or co-ownership is encouraged.
Privacy, accuracy, cost, regulatory acceptance, data quality.
Digital-first insurers and aggregators (Policybazaar, Acko, Digit); online policy purchase; e-insurance account (EIA) to hold policies electronically; digital KYC.
A market where shares, bonds, derivatives and other securities are issued and traded. Provides capital to companies and investment avenues to investors; indicator of economic health.
Trading of already-issued securities among investors through exchanges.
Equity shares, preference shares, bonds, debentures, G-secs, T-bills, derivatives (futures and options), mutual fund units, ETFs, REITs, InvITs.

flashcards.back: Nifty Next 50, Nifty Bank, Nifty IT, Nifty Midcap, BSE 500. Index construction: weighted by free-float market capitalisation.
Rising vs falling markets; circuit breakers (market-wide 10%, 15%, 20%) and price bands stop panic movements.
Large-cap (top 100), mid-cap (101–250), small-cap (251st onward).

Insider trading, price manipulation (pump and dump, circular trading), front running, Ponzi schemes, fake advisors/tips (Telegram/WhatsApp), unauthorised trading, misuse of client funds, IPO frauds, "algo" scams, mule accounts and fake trading apps.

Dealing in securities by someone with unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI) — banned under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI Act; penalties include fine up to Rs 25 crore or three times the profit, imprisonment up to 10 years.

Stock exchanges and SEBI use AI-based surveillance systems to analyse order patterns, anomaly detection for abnormal volumes/prices before announcements, network (graph) analysis to link related accounts, NLP on news, social media and filings, alerts for unusual trading, early-warning systems, risk-based supervision, ASM/GSM…

Use registered brokers and advisers (SEBI RIA/RA), verify through SEBI's database, never give login credentials/OTP, UPI handle ending @valid for brokers (verified handles), 2FA, enable trading alerts, Investor Protection Fund (IPF), investor grievance redressal through SCORES/ODR.

Trading account (to place buy/sell orders with the broker) + Demat account (to hold) + Bank account (to settle funds) — the 3-in-1 account. Basic Services Demat Account (BSDA) for small investors with lower charges.

Shares are bought and sold on the same day (square off before market close); no delivery; uses margin/leverage; high risk, high turnover; brokerage is lower; taxed as speculative business income at slab rates.
F&O (futures and options), BTST/STBT, margin trading facility (MTF), short selling, algo trading, commodity and currency trading.
Market order, limit order, stop-loss order, AMO (after-market order), IOC (immediate or cancel), GTT (good till triggered).
STT (Securities Transaction Tax), GST on brokerage, stamp duty, SEBI turnover fee, exchange transaction charges.

flashcards.back: Growth, income, balanced/ liquid, tax-saving.
Direct (no distributor commission; lower expense ratio) vs Regular; Growth vs IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal; formerly dividend).
36 categories to standardise (equity 10, debt 16, hybrid 6, solution-oriented 2, other 2).
Expense ratio (annual fee as % of AUM), exit load (fee on early redemption), stamp duty, STT on equity funds.
MF gives diversification and professional management; direct stocks provide control but need research and carry concentrated risk.
Bought 100 units of a mutual fund at NAV Rs 20 (Rs 2,000), sold at NAV Rs 26 (Rs 2,600): ROI = (600 ÷ 2,000) × 100 = 30%.
Bought 50 shares at Rs 400 (Rs 20,000); received dividends of Rs 500; sold at Rs 460 (Rs 23,000): ROI = (3,000 + 500) ÷ 20,000 × 100 = 17.5%.

Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals (monthly) in a mutual fund. Benefits: discipline, rupee-cost averaging (more units when NAV is low, fewer when NAV is high), power of compounding, no need to time the market, start with small sums (Rs 100–500).
FV = P × [((1 + i)n − 1) ÷ i] × (1 + i), where P = monthly instalment, i = monthly rate of return (annual ÷ 12), n = number of months.
Invest Rs 1,000 per month; NAV = 10, 8, 12 → units = 100, 125, 83.33 → total 308.33 units for Rs 3,000; average cost = Rs 9.73 per unit (less than average NAV of Rs 10).
Lump sum good when markets are low and the investor has a surplus; SIP spreads risk over time.
